successors.name: Kushan Empire
successors.text: Cliopatria's Kushan shape of 51-90 contains the whole Ferghana basin (168 of the 172 cells of the last Great Yuan shape)

successors.name: Kangju
successors.text: 'By this time it had gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana' (the Hanshu, 206 BCE-23 CE, per the Kangju page)

capitals.name: Guishan (Kuishan; Khujand in the page's brackets); Ershi in the Han accounts of the siege

ledger.x: 128 BC: Zhang Qian finds the kingdom of Dayuan in Ferghana.
102 BC: Li Guangli's second army reaches Dayuan.
101 BC: the nobles of Dayuan kill their king and buy peace.
50: Cliopatria's Great Yuan row ends and the Kushan shape of 51 covers Ferghana.

wars.name: War of the Heavenly Horses
wars.outcome: Han victory: after a 40-day siege of the capital the nobles killed King Wugua and gave Li Guangli about 3,000 horses; a pro-Han king, Meicai, was enthroned and Dayuan became a puppet state of Han.

certainty.note: A small oasis kingdom in a mountain basin: the pages give no frontier, only cities and neighbours by direction (Kangju to the north-west, the Wusun and Yuezhi beyond).
